title: Two Italian cipher letters to Ottavio Piccolomini, c. 1646 (catalogue 2358; SOA Zámrsk, RA Piccolomini inv. 24874 and 24876): Vlnas's 2017 key for the neighbouring inv. 24873 applied; both letters read in part, writer not identified

system.summary: Consonants written plain; vowels as odd digits a e i o u = 1 3 5 7 9 (u also v); even digits 2 4 6 8 (and 0) and the plain letters a e i o u w x y are nulls (Vlnas 2017, table 3).
system.sibling_key: Vlnas 2017 table 3, recovered by Vlnas from inv. 24873 (same microfilm run; 24874 likely the same writer by hand and content); used unchanged.
system.notes: distinct_symbols: tokens in the two transcriptions (digits 0-9, consonant letters, the class tokens S and G, R apart from r, and the plain null letters). nulls.count: null signs that occur (2 4 6 8 0 a e u w). On these photographs the digit 5 and the letter s, and the digit 9 and the letters g and q, have the same shape: the transcription writes class tokens S and G, and the reading chooses by sense (77 such choices in the read words of 24874, 29 in 24876). In this hand 6 is also close to b and t (two repairs in 24874). key_order: the odd digits run in vowel order.

prior_solution.where: No reading of inv. 24874 or 24876 found: Vlnas 2017 (appendix B21, B22: not deciphered, no text printed), the catalogue vetting of 6 Nov 2026 (DECODE dumps, Lasry's list, Tomokiyo, HistoCrypt 2018) and a web search. Vlnas 2017 ch. 4.2 deciphers the neighbouring inv. 24873 and prints the key used here.

solution.what: Frames 24873, 24873_1, 24873_2, 24874 and 24876 taken from the appendix zip of Vlnas 2017 (theses.cz/id/p3p2kb); the thesis read for the key (table 3) and for what it prints.
Vlnas 2017, the catalogue vetting record (DECODE dumps, Lasry, Tomokiyo, HistoCrypt 2018) and one web search: no edition or decipherment of 24874 or 24876 found.
Sign conventions written before any value was applied (class tokens S for s/5 and G for g/q/9); each letter transcribed twice from different crops and reconciled on the image.

Vlnas's table 3 (from inv. 24873) frozen in key_frozen.tsv with our additions (0 null, f long s, class tokens) and applied unchanged to 24874 and 24876; even digits and plain vowel letters behave as nulls throughout.

Frozen key applied to an excerpt of the 24873_2 postscript, which Vlnas did not print: the 14 groups chosen by the solver all give Italian (desidera Sua Altezza ... ragguaglio ... che venendo). Weak: selected and self-scored, no external decipherment to grade against, the freeze rests on file times.
Both letters decrypted with key.tsv and read with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py fails on any unmarked departure. English translations made.

Independent check (VERIFY.md): blind copy of 11 lines (357 signs) of the two letters and 2 held-out lines before the solver's files were opened; about 7 solver errors and 15 unresolved signs; key and statuses confirmed. Found three places in 24874 where the transcription had followed the sense against the passes, and asked for strict counts and an honest account of the held-out excerpt.

After the check: 24874 L09 and L12 written as the passes saw them (6, l; a blotted sign as [?]); three missed or misread null signs added in 24876. politico and avertimenti are now marked repairs; 24874 verbatim fell from 78 to 76 of 116.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: V. Vlnas's key (2017, ch. 4.2, table 3), recovered by him from the neighbouring letter inv. 24873 and not applied by him to 24874 or 24876 (his appendix B21, B22), was applied unchanged to both letters; our additions are 0 as a null, f as long s and class tokens for the s/5 and g/q/9 homographs.
outcome.fraction_read_source: scripts/check_marks.py: 108 of 166 words verbatim from the signs (24874: 76 of 116, 65.5%; 24876: 32 of 50, 64.0%); with no s/i or g/q/u/v class choice 47 of 166 (33 and 14). Marked repairs (6 and 4) are not counted as read.

texts.label: inv. 24874 (Vlnas 2017 appendix B21)
texts.summary: The writer, reporting for someone he calls 'l'arciduca mio signore', says that His Highness took great consolation from Piccolomini's letter and wishes a just and full report on the military and political government, since Piccolomini knows best which advices are needed; the clear tail announces the coming of Don Miguel de Salamanca. Archduke Leopold Wilhelm was named governor of the Spanish Netherlands at the end of 1646, which fits, but the text does not name him.
texts.note: Words 116: 76 verbatim from the signs (65.5%), of which 33 with no s/i or g/q/u/v class choice; 6 with a marked repair; 7 guessed from context; 27 holes. L01-L03 are mostly holes. 'dal' (L09) rests on a doubtful sign.

texts.label: inv. 24876 (Vlnas 2017 appendix B22)
texts.summary: Two cipher passages between clear news: Bavaria, 'so that we must fight', complaints already answered; and 'the Duke of Bavaria wants peace by all means, so that he can consider the advantage we shall have'. The clear text reports prisoners' news of the enemy and, from Vienna, a journey to Linz and then Ratisbona. Fits Bavaria's moves toward a separate truce in late 1646 (Ulm, March 1647); context only.
texts.note: Words 50: 32 verbatim from the signs (64.0%), of which 14 with no class choice; 4 with a marked repair; 2 guessed; 12 holes. Another hand than 24874, same key.

texts.label: inv. 24873_2, cipher postscript (excerpt; letter of the key source)
texts.summary: An excerpt of 14 groups of the postscript, which Vlnas did not print: 'desidera Sua Altezza [il] ragguaglio ... sono come ancora lei ... che venendo ... se ne possa governare'.
texts.note: Held-out excerpt chosen and scored by the solver; weak evidence, not a blind score. Frame 24873 itself is deciphered in Vlnas 2017 and not reproduced here.
